reviewScope: Root inspected all thirteen eight-direction paired source/serving contact sheets (208 main frame panels), detailed full-resolution views where needed, the separate sixteen-panel font rear-lit diagnostic and all ten final opening thumbnails. works.independentVisualDecision: All four sculpted outer faces are present and correspond to the four Thorvaldsens Museum A555 plaster-model relief compositions. Full-size native and production diagnostic views resolve the dark Three Hovering Angels face: three heads, joined arms, wings and legs are retained. No missing head or face capture was observed. The unrecorded floor-contact underside is an explicitly disclosed mounting limitation.
captureScope: Uneven capture lighting and cool/dark source texture persist; the Three Hovering Angels face is substantially darker than the other faces, even when turned toward the production key light. No material recoloring was requested.

The mounting/floor-contact underside is unrecorded. The underside view exposes backfaces/interior texture rather than a documented closed bottom; do not present this as a measured or complete underside.
The bottom floor-contact perimeter is mildly jagged. This localized mounting edge does not remove any sculpted face, head or limb.
Top rim and circular floral collar are retained. This visual review does not establish an accurately measured working basin depth.
Assembly is counted once; its four component reliefs are not separate additions.

works.diagnosticPoseQualification: The rear-lit diagnostic uses yaw180 solely to move Three Hovering Angels to the +Z lit FRONT view. Source and preview asset hashes and appearance hash equal the neutral review. This diagnostic pose is not the final delivered opening recommendation.

holds.reason: The rear and top of the head contain a large irregular opening, while a long jagged missing strip runs down the back/drapery with exposed interior and stray colored surfaces. The frontal likeness matches A164, but a coherent complete captured head/back is not established. This is a freestanding figure, so the gap is not the expected unrecorded mounting back of a wall relief.

Full-resolution overhead source image shows most of the crown/top of the head as an open crater with a jagged rim below the hairline and visible hollow interior. The frontal body/dress/basket are coherent and match A179, but the missing cranial surface is not justified by documentation of the physical plaster.

Overhead and side views expose a wide opening through the rear/top of the cap/head, with uncaptured gaps around the body/support interior and irregular extended base flaps. The eagle and frontal group match A44, but the missing head surface prevents acceptance as a complete freestanding capture.
